パレスサイクリング

Palace Cycling

Tokyo, Japan · Chiyoda (Imperial Palace, Uchibori-dori) · Open streets · Social

Family

パレスサイクリング is an open-streets program in Tokyo, Japan: streets closed to cars and open to bikes. It runs every Sunday from 10:00 am local time. Pace: not a race course: the organizers ask riders to keep speeds down and pass only when it is safe.

For visitors

No sign-up. Free loaner bikes (about 70, adult city bikes down to kids' bikes) from 10:00 am to 3:30 pm, back by 4:00 pm, one lap per loan; you register on your phone with a QR code at the tent. Since March 2026 you must get off and walk the U-turn at the Hirakawa-mon crossing. Cars come back at 4:00 pm sharp.

First time? Here's the drill

Bring
a helmet, water, a spare tube or patch kit, a way to pay for the stop.
Arrive
Ten or fifteen minutes before 10:00 am. Tell whoever's leading that you're new.
Pace
Pace: not a race course: the organizers ask riders to keep speeds down and pass only when it is safe.
Check
Look at the host's website the day of — that's where cancellations, weather calls and start changes get posted.

About the パレスサイクリング group ride

Every Sunday the road along the Imperial Palace moat closes to cars and opens to bikes: a flat 3 km out-and-back between Iwaidabashi and Hirakawa-mon. It is a family course, not a training loop; kids, tandems and tourists share it and staff ask fast riders to ease off. Free loaner bikes since April 2026 make it an easy first ride in Tokyo.
